principle: MOVING-SUPPORT CAPTURE IS A SUPPORT-TOPOLOGY TRANSFER: FEET MUST EARN TRANSLATING OWNERSHIP BEFORE THE FINAL LADDER CONTACT RELEASES.
quality_thesis: The root begins stationary on ladder support, a foot captures a moving deck at a stable deck-relative anchor, ladder ownership peels away asymmetrically without a support gap, the last hand becomes a pivot while translation is inherited, then released velocity creates an overlong first deck catch followed by shorter corrections and delayed upper-body settle.

novelty.new_causality: Unlike Locomotion020's moving-frame EXIT, 026 performs the opposite support-topology problem without reverse interpolation: a stationary vertical support hands the body into a translating horizontal support through mixed hand+foot ownership, last-hand pivot, velocity inheritance, and displaced deck-relative recovery.

quality_history.defect: K10-K12 recovery remained visibly over-stretched: planted feet outran root/COM so the settle read as a dragged mannequin rather than paid capture debt.
quality_history.correction: Advance K10-K12 root/COM onto the moving support, re-author shorter deck-relative foot anchors, and preserve decreasing 15→12→10 px root spacing plus delayed arm settle.

quality_history.basis: Actual corrected render inspected: stationary ladder ownership transfers through mixed right-platform capture and last-hand pivot without a support gap; the platform visibly pulls the released root into an overlong first catch; K10→K12 recovery brings COM/root back over translating support with 15→12→10 px corrective debt and delayed arm settle.

Same actual final render/full specimen. Taste: memorable inbound support-topology transfer rather than generic gait. Function: deck-relative support anchors, last-hand pivot, inherited translation, overlong catch, shorter corrections, and delayed settle are visible and mechanically coherent. Contempt: the result cannot be reproduced by merely linearly connecting endpoint poses because decisive mixed-ownership and recovery keys carry causal load.
